תנו רבנן (61a.16-61b.1): the Tosefta on the proven amulet and how it is worn
והתניא (61b.2): a proven amulet is one that healed three people as one

props.gloss_en: the mishna: nor [may one go out] with an amulet when it is not from an expert
Rav Pappa: do not say [one may go out only] when both the man is an expert and the amulet is proven
Rav Pappa: rather, once the man is an expert, even though the amulet is not proven [one may go out with it]
the Tosefta: what is a proven amulet? any that healed, and again, and a third time
the Tosefta: [this holds] alike for a written amulet and an amulet of roots
the Tosefta: [this holds] alike for a sick person in danger and a sick person not in danger
the Tosefta: not [only for] one who has been seized [by the falling sickness], but [also] so that he not be seized
the Tosefta: and he ties and unties [the amulet] even in the public domain
the Tosefta: provided he does not tie it onto a bracelet or a ring and go out with it in the public domain
the Tosefta: because of how it appears to the eye
the baraita: what is a proven amulet? any that healed three people as one
this [baraita, three people] is for proving the man
that [Tosefta, healed and again and a third time] is for proving the amulet
Rav Pappa: three amulets for three men, three times each -- the man is proven
Rav Pappa: [in that case] the amulet is proven too
Rav Pappa: three amulets for three men, once each -- the man is proven
Rav Pappa: [in that case] the amulet is proven (denied: it is not proven)
Rav Pappa: one amulet for three men -- the amulet is proven
Rav Pappa: [in that case] the man is proven (denied: he is not proven)
Rav Pappa: three amulets for one man -- the amulet is proven (denied: it is certainly not proven)
[proposed:] the question whether amulets have sanctity bears on rescuing them from a fire
the baraita: blessings and amulets, though they contain letters and many matters of the Torah, are not rescued from a fire but are burned in their place

questions.gloss_en: Rav Pappa's question: three amulets that healed one man -- is the writer proven? do we say 'it healed him', or perhaps it is this patient's mazal that takes to the writing? -- left standing (teiku)

supports.gloss_en: דיקא נמי, דקתני ולא בקמיע בזמן שאינו מן המומחה, ולא קתני בזמן שאינו מומחה. שמע מינה -- the mishna speaks of the writer's expertise, not the amulet's

objections.gloss_en: והתניא: איזהו קמיע מומחה -- כל שריפא שלשה בני אדם כאחד! -- a proven amulet is one that healed three different people, not one person three times

answered_by.gloss_en: לא קשיא: הא לממחויי גברא, הא לממחויי קמיעא -- three people prove the writer; one person thrice proves the amulet (= p_ok_lemachuyei_gavra, p_ok_lemachuyei_kamea)

objections.gloss_en: תא שמע: הברכות והקמיעין ... אין מצילין אותן מפני הדליקה ונשרפים במקומן -- rescue from fire is already decided, so the question cannot turn on it
